# Observability and evaluation

Read this when someone will operate or grade the graph. A graph nobody can trace is a graph whose
failures are attributed to the wrong owner; a graph nobody evaluates at the path level is graded on
its happy path. Section 13 of the artifact carries both plans.

## Contents

- Lineage identity
- Events to emit
- Indicators and failure planes
- Content, redaction, and retention
- Evaluation plan
- Alerts and runbook branches

## Lineage identity

Every span and event carries: run ID, node ID, edge ID, attempt ID, retry/replay marker, and the
**authoritative-final-result** marker that distinguishes the result the graph adopted from the
attempts it discarded. Generic GenAI telemetry conventions are still in development and do not
supply a workflow attempt field, so the design names its own attempt identity rather than assuming
a standard one exists.
*[sourced: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions at
[`56d6b11`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/tree/56d6b11a02129319bf371083fa134b7ce989c976),
reviewed 2026-08-23]*

## Events to emit

| Event class | Minimum fields |
|---|---|
| Node start/end | node class, attempt, duration, outcome, budget consumed |
| Tool call | tool identity and revision, argument digest, validation result, duration, outcome |
| Handoff | source, destination, packet digest, taint labels carried |
| Guardrail | which guardrail, at which boundary, decision, and what it blocked |
| Approval | approver identity, candidate identity, decision, expiry, resumed-state check result |
| Checkpoint | checkpoint ID, schema version, boundary, write confirmation |
| Effect | key, attempt, dispatch, receipt, reconciliation result, `UNKNOWN` age |
| Admission and shed | queue, tenant, priority, decision, reason |
| Cancel | cooperative signal time, durable persist time, in-flight disposition |

## Indicators and failure planes

Measure and attribute separately — one aggregate success rate hides the owner:

| Plane | Indicators |
|---|---|
| Control plane | schedule-to-start latency, queue depth and oldest-item age, admission and shed rates, stuck-run count |
| Workers | heartbeat age, lease expiries, poison-work backlog, hot shards, per-tenant share |
| Model provider | invalid tool-argument rate, path divergence from expected routes, retry and timeout rate, token and cost per run |
| Checkpoint or history store | checkpoint age, write failures, replay divergence, restore drills |
| Effect targets | `UNKNOWN` effects awaiting reconciliation, reconciliation latency, compensation rate |
| Human control | approval wait time, expired approvals, rejection rate |
| Run outcomes | success and consistency rate across repeats, cancellation latency, budget exhaustion |

## Content, redaction, and retention

Prompt, input, and output content is opt-in, redacted at capture, retention-bound, and
cardinality-controlled. Taint labels on content are recorded as attributes so a reviewer can see
that untrusted input reached a node without reading the input itself.

## Evaluation plan

Separate the lanes and report each with its numerator and denominator:

| Level | What it proves | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Node | A node meets its own contract | Fixed inputs, schema validation, grader per node |
| Edge | Routing selects the allowed destination | Deterministic edges by assertion; model-selected edges by trials against the allowed set |
| Path | The graph takes the expected route for a class of input | Trace comparison against an expected path with tolerance stated |
| Outcome | The final output meets the consumer's criteria | Task/trial/grader with a threshold |
| Recovery | Resume and replay behave as designed | Kill at each checkpoint boundary and resume; replay recorded histories on the new build |
| Consistency | Repeated runs agree | N trials on the same input; report agreement rate |
| Temporal | Timeouts, cancellation, expiry fire as specified | Injected delays and cancel signals |
| Budget | Bounds hold | Runs at the edge of each budget; verify the stop and its evidence |

Activation and routing, artifact quality, and runtime behaviour are three different results.
Static design evidence never upgrades runtime evidence: durability, provider behaviour, and effect
safety stay `[unverified]` until the approved implementation is exercised. Changing a case, grader,
threshold, or candidate creates a new candidate rather than extending a pass.

## Alerts and runbook branches

Each failure class needs a different response, so the runbook branches on it: model failure, tool
failure, join starvation, approval timeout, checkpoint failure, effect uncertainty (`UNKNOWN`
backlog), scheduler backlog, and budget exhaustion. An alert that says "workflow failed" without the
class pages the wrong person.
